messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: tailored availability annex + order-form language for ZenithHealth

Ben / Marissa,

ZenithHealth procurement sent an RFI this morning and flagged three items that will need custom language attached to the MSA / SOW and mirrored in the order form:

- Availability: they want a 99.99% uptime commitment for their primary region with explicit credit schedule and a tolerance window for maintenance; they also asked about regional failover.
- Latency: they asked for a p95 latency commitment for embedding lookups (called out as 100ms p95).
- Evidence & retention: audit log retention for 7 years (exportable), plus SOC 2 attestation and a request for historical latency percentiles for the last 90 days.

I attached the RFI and my rough outline (initial_sla_outline.docx). Can you draft a targeted "Availability Annex" and suggested redlines to our order-form language that we can send to procurement? Key constraints: we cannot commit to 100ms p95 at scale without a defined TPS bound or dedicated capacity—if necessary we should propose an alternate path (dedicated pool + quantization/ops play) with a fall-back credit schedule.

Target: have a first draft to send externally by EOD Monday (1/18). If you need to loop in infra/legal for technical wording or evidence packaging, call it out in your draft.

Thanks,
Grace

Subject: Draft: Availability Annex and order-form suggestions (for review)

Hi Tom / ZenithHealth team,

Thanks for the clear RFI — appreciated. Per our call last week I've attached a first-pass Availability Annex and a small set of order-form edits intended to map to the MSA and SOW attachment you referenced. Highlights:

- Proposed availability commitment: 99.95% uptime for primary region with defined recovery/notification SLAs and a documented failover policy; an optional Dedicated Pool addendum to purchase 99.99% with defined throughput bounds.
- Latency: we did not hard-commit a blanket 100ms p95 for embeddings; instead we propose a performance-tiered guarantee tied to a documented throughput envelope (example: p95 <= 150ms for embedding lookups at <= 50 TPS on Standard hosting; tighter guarantees available with Dedicated).
- Evidence & retention: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and an audit-log export (CSV) with a 7-year retention option for customers on enterprise plans; operational cost and export controls noted in the annex.

Next steps: please review the attached draft_availability_annex.pdf and call out the items you want tightened. If you want the 99.99% availability lane we can price a Dedicated Pool order form and provide a quantified credit schedule.

I've included Grace and Marissa from our team to help coordinate legal redlines and procurement routing. Happy to set a short working session next week to walk the annex line-by-line.

Best,

From: Procurement Team <procurement@zenithhealth.com>

Cc: ZenithHealth Legal <legal@zenithhealth.com>, IT Compliance <it-compliance@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 14:45:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Availability Annex and order-form suggestions (for review)

Ben,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft. A few clarifications/concerns from our side before we proceed to legal redlines: 

1) Latency guarantee: ZenithHealth's internal SLAs for latency are strict because of real-time decisioning workflows. We specifically asked for 100ms p95 for embedding lookups; the proposed tiered approach is acceptable only if we can get a) a clear definition of measurement (rolling 24h window, agent-level traces), b) an objective test harness and c) credits if guarantees are missed.

2) Availability: 99.95% is a downgrade from our ask of 99.99%. If that higher bar requires Dedicated capacity, we need a fixed SKU and pricing and a clear transition path (how long to provision, expected queueing/lag during migration).

3) Retention: 7-year audit log retention raises data residency and cost questions — we need to understand export formats, encryption-at-rest policies, and any cross-border transfer implications. Also confirm whether logs will include request-level token payloads or only metadata.

4) Evidence: we will need access to SOC 2 Type II report and a mechanized way to validate recent latency percentiles (links to dashboards or a one-off export).

Please respond to the above points; if you can propose concrete language for credits and measurement we can expedite legal review.

Regards,
Tom Nguyen
Sr. Procurement Manager — ZenithHealth
procurement@zenithhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 08:09:45 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Procurement questions — proposed path and next steps (ZenithHealth)

Grace / Marissa,

Forwarding Zenith's reply and my proposed approach. Key points and recommended responses: 

- Latency measurement: propose a concrete measurement clause: p95 measured at the service edge over a rolling 24-hour window using production telemetry; establish a test harness run by Zenith (we provide an agreed load profile) for validation. Offer two options: (A) Standard hosting: guarantee p95 <= 150ms for embeddings at defined TPS with credits; (B) Dedicated SKU: 100ms p95 at capacity bounds (priced).

- Availability: propose a dual-option order-form entry: 99.95% (standard) and 99.99% (dedicated add-on). For 99.99% include provisioning timeline (15 business days) and defined throughput for the dedicated pool. Include a clear credit schedule for each decrement band.

- Retention & evidence: confirm we can offer exportable audit logs (CSV/JSON) and SOC 2 Type II report; call out that payload-level request content is captured only if customer opts in (and subject to export controls). Recommend we provide a one-off 90-day latency percentile export and a read-only dashboard link for ongoing monitoring (we can provide a secure link and a short TTL token for their IT team).

I drafted language in zenith_sla_proposal_v2.pdf attached with suggested credit tables and a mock Dedicated SKU. I propose we: 1) send this refined proposal to Zenith by end of day Thursday 1/21, 2) schedule a 30-min working session with their procurement + legal + our solutions engineer to walk measurement definitions, and 3) route the Dedicated SKU to pricing if they opt for 99.99%.

If you're good with the approach I'll send the updated package externally and book the session.

Thanks,
Ben
